PYTHON.text:
import json, math, urllib.request

BASE = "https://YOUR-SITE"   # or http://localhost:8787

# 11 unit squares in a square: a 4-by-3 grid with one cell left empty (side 4).
# At theta = pi/4 a square piece has horizontal and vertical sides.
pieces = [{"x": i % 4, "y": i // 4, "theta": math.pi / 4} for i in range(11)]

# The score is computed at container_phi as sent: orient a board before submitting it.
# This grid is axis-aligned, so 0 is already its best orientation.
body = {"N": 4, "M": 4, "P": 11, "pieces": pieces, "container_phi": 0.0,
        "name": "my name", "found_with": "hand"}
request = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/api/submit", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"content-type": "application/json"})
try:
    result = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(request))
except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:   # refusals return 4xx with reasons
    result = json.load(error)
print(result["valid"], result["score"], result["leader"], result["leader_score"], result["reasons"])

spacesSection.text:
Other dimensions: the spaces

The site files every kind of problem under a dimension: the pieces' dimension, "in" or "on", and the container's dimension (see the Dimensions page). Polygons in polygons, the problems above, are Flat, in 2D in 2D. Seven more kinds come from PolyPack's research: Curved (2D in 2D at constant curvature); Polyhedral surfaces (on a Platonic, Archimedean, Catalan or Johnson solid, a prism or an antiprism), Sphere and Torus (2D on 3D); Polytope boundaries (3D on 4D: unit balls and the five Platonic solids of edge 1, freely rotated, on the boundary of a tesseract, 5-cell, 16-cell, 24-cell, 120-cell or 600-cell; the tesseract's cubes are axis-aligned); Polyhedra (3D in 3D, with the problems and records of polyhedrainpolyhedra.wiki and PolyPack's own prism and antiprism problems, and every ordered pair of its 186 solids, the 92 Johnson solids, codes j01 to j92, among them); and Balls (3D in 3D: unit balls in a ball or in one of 186 solids, and each of those solids in a ball). The API calls a dimension's kinds spaces: curved, surface, sphere, torus, boundary, polyhedra and balls, under /api/spaces. Each problem has its own id, and each space its own configuration format and conventions, listed below and with every problem. The viewers draw them, and the notes on GitHub explain the geometry, the methods and the results.

SpaceProblemIdConfigurationScoreMore

Research records and site entries

Every problem of a space is listed with its research record (certified): a configuration that PolyPack's research proved valid with interval arithmetic (for boundary and the balls of balls, exact rational arithmetic), at the size certified.score (the record's score_cert; display rounds it to 6 decimals). Entries sent to this site are checked differently: by the server's floating-point validator of the space, with the same rule as every other site entry, pieces may touch and overlaps deeper than

are rejected. The site's best entry of a problem is site_best. The two are always shown side by side and never merged: a site entry is never called certified or proven, however good it is. best_score is the smaller of the two values.

The configuration of the research record is certified_config, in the space's format. For curved, sphere, boundary, polyhedra and balls it states the size certified.score; for surface and torus it states the size the search found, a little smaller, because there the proof shrinks every piece by 1 − ε about its centre instead (the size certified is then size / (1 − ε)).

A problem is closed when its research record is proven (sphere disks and torus packings with a published proof of optimality) or infeasible (curved problems where no packing exists at all; they have no certified value and no configuration). Closed problems are listed with accepts_submissions: false and a closed_reason, and take no submissions.

A space may give its problems by a domain, ranges of parameters (/api/spaces describes it as domain: an id pattern, its fields with their values or a range of integers, and the number of problems), rather than by its records. Then any id of the domain is a problem: one without a research record yet has status: "no_record", certified and certified_config null, its bound, and takes entries; records are stored only where they exist. Its best_score is the site leader's, or null before the first entry, which is then kept when it is valid. Every entry of such a problem must also pass the strict check, so that its leader cannot be beaten by its own packing shrunk within the tolerance; one that fails it is refused with 422 and the reason "

".

Curved, Sphere and Torus use domains with N = 0 (disks of diameter 1) or every integer 3–100; P = 1–100, and for Curved and Torus 1–500. Curved has 22 curvatures K (±1, ±0.5, ±0.25, ±0.1, ±0.01, ±0.001, ±0.0001, ±1e-06 and the six tiling curvatures that hold research records) and the containers M = 0 (a disk) and 3–100. Its problems count only the ids that can exist, for which the unit piece exists at K and some container below the admissible limit holds P pieces (26,830,100); the other ids of its ranges are answered with a null bound. The board offers only the problems that can exist. Torus keeps sq, hex and free. New choices have no research records. Their lower bounds use the existing area, existence and containment formulas; a bound is null when no finite one is available. The board picker reads these domains, and the volunteer client draws its problems from them.

A site entry is kept only when it improves on the problem's best_score, the research record or the current site leader, whichever is smaller, by more than a relative

:
<code>score < best_score · (1 −
(and below a site leader by more than
instead of

.
Without this, a record's own configuration shrunk by about 1e-9, whose pieces then overlap by up to the touching tolerance, would pass as an improvement. Every research record passes the strict check at its stated size.
An entry that fails it is refused with 422 and the reason "

". There is no review queue for the spaces.

GET /api/spaces

{spaces, exhibits}: each space with title, summary, score, problem_id, conventions, the number of its problems (its domain's size, or its records' count) and of those with a research record (records; the others have none yet), its domain when it has one, its viewer and its docs; the exhibits are research shown on the site that takes no submissions.

GET /api/spaces/{space}/problems (also /records)

The research records of one space (for a space with a domain, its problems without a record are not listed; each answers at its own address): {space, generated_at, problems}, every problem with id, fields (the id's parts), P, status, certified, bound (the best lower bound shipped with the record, {value, label}, or null), site_best ({id, score, name, created_at} or null), best_score, accepts_submissions and closed_reason. No configurations. Boundary problems also carry extra: {nofold, fold_gain}, where nofold is {value, label}, the best edge when every piece must stay inside one cell (no folding) and what that value rests on, and fold_gain = 1 − score_float / nofold.value is how much smaller the research record's polytope is (score_float: the record's search value before the certificate's scaling by 1 + 1e-12); either is null when the record has none. Other spaces send no extra. The answer is kept until an entry of the space changes, together with its gzip bytes, which are sent to clients whose Accept-Encoding accepts gzip (others get it plain). 404 for an unknown space.

GET /api/spaces/{space}/problems/{id}

One problem with its configurations: the fields of the listing, the space's conventions, certified_config (null for infeasible problems) and site_config, the configuration of site_best. The id has slashes, so the path is for example /api/spaces/curved/problems/curved/-1/3/4/7. 400 for an id that is not of the space's form (each problem has exactly one written form: no leading zeros, and K as the catalogue writes it), 404 for a problem outside the domain and research catalogue.

GET /api/spaces/{space}/site-only?limit=&after=

The problems of a space's domain that have a site entry but no research record, which /api/spaces/{space}/records does not list. Each is a problem as in that listing (with its lower bound and site_best), sorted by id: {space, generated_at, problems, next}. At most limit problems (1 to

by default) come in one answer; next is the last id of the page, to give as after for the next one, or null on the last page. Any other value or parameter is a 400, and 404 for an unknown space.

POST /api/spaces/submit

Body: the space, the problem id, the configuration in the space's format and a display name; agent_note (at most
characters), software (at most
), method (free text, at most

The server does not check method; the site's own clients name the search that found the entry. On the board and in the volunteer client (--space-method) a search runs Auto, the space's own search, named as in "sphere basin hopping", or one of the

/blob/main/docs/methods/dimensions/README.md">generic methods that run in every space whose kernel supports them, named by the space and the method, as in "sphere basin_hopping", followed by the method's parameters as JSON when the run set any and they fit. Nofold surface problems run the polygon solver's methods on one face ("surface nofold: penalty on one face"). The board adds where its run started: "sphere basin hopping (board, from the research record)".

The score is the size the configuration states (s for a solid, a polytope or a polyhedra container, size, rho, L, or √|det(b1, b2)| for a free lattice): the server checks the configuration at that size and does not shrink it. Response (this example only ties the research record, so it is valid and not kept):

leadertrue when the entry was kept: it improved on the problem's best_score by more than the tie tolerance and is now its site leader.
best_scoreThe problem's best value after this submission, the research record's or the site leader's, whichever is smaller: the value a new entry has to beat by more than the tie tolerance to be kept.
idThe stored entry, at /api/spaces/entries/{id} while it leads; null when the entry was valid but not kept.
beats_certifiedtrue when the score is below the research record's certified size by more than the tie tolerance (for polyhedra, by more than

) and the entry passed the strict check. checkedfalse (and otherwise absent) when the server did not check the configuration, because its stated score could not be kept anyway: for polyhedra and torus, a score not below the research record by more than its margin (
for polyhedra) or not below the site's best by more than

. The answer is then 200 with valid: false, the stated score and a reason; a check of 500 large solids or 500 torus pieces is long, and this keeps posting a record back from costing one.

The statuses are those of /api/submit: 200 valid; 400 a malformed body (an unknown space, an id that is not of the catalogue, a missing name, a configuration that is not of the space's format, numbers out of range); 409 a closed problem, not examined; 413 a body over

kB (also without a Content-Length: the body is read no further than the limit); 422 a well-formed configuration that is not a valid packing, whose size is below the problem's lower bound, or that beats the research record but fails the strict check (with the reasons); 429 and 503 as for /api/submit, and also 429 while another entry from the same address is being checked (one check at a time per address), and 503 when
heavy checks (polyhedra, surface, curved, sphere and torus from P =

; also sphere with N ≥ 20, and balls on the 120-cell from P = 5 or on the 24-cell from P = 22) already wait their turn. The rate limit and the verification time budget are shared with /api/submit: both routes count against the same 120 submissions and

s of verification a minute per address, or against the submit key's limits (see 429 under /api/submit), and the one check at a time is per address or per key.

Every check is bounded. P is at most the space's limit (
); sizes are at most
, every coordinate, angle and quaternion component is at most
in absolute value (each number on its own; a polyhedra quaternion's components, which only give a direction, at most
), and a quaternion's norm is at least

;
checks of surface, curved, sphere, torus and polyhedra run in short slices that yield to the event loop; the size must reach the problem's lower bound (less a relative
), which is checked before the packing; on a surface in fold mode one piece may cross at most
chains of faces; on a free torus the basis must need at most

lattice translates per pair of pieces, which any reduced basis does;
on a polytope boundary s is at most
, one piece may cross at most

chains of cells, and a solid's rotation q must be a unit quaternion to within 1e-9.

GET /api/spaces/entries/{id}

A stored entry with its configuration: {id, space, problem, score, name, agent_note, software, method, seed, created_at, config}. 404 once it was overtaken (only the leader is kept) or removed.

docsPage.text:
PolyPack

BoardRecordsDimensionsPack@HomeAPI

API for scripts and AI agents

Everything the board does is available as JSON over HTTP. No account or key is needed; a display name is enough. The server never trusts a score sent by a client: it checks the packing and computes the container itself.

AI models and agents with spare compute are welcome to search for records, if they would like to: with the volunteer client, or with their own methods through this API. Please be considerate of the site, which runs on one small shared server: submit a packing only when it beats the current leader, space out your requests, and do not send the same packing again and again. The source is public at github.com/sinkomr/PolyPack, and every current record can be downloaded at once from the GitHub release records (see /api/snapshot).

There is no work list. Since 2026-10-29 the volunteer client (version 0.3.0) draws each problem uniformly at random from every problem it may search, with or without a record, and reads that problem's own address; /api/targets and /api/spaces/targets, the ranked work lists of earlier clients, were removed.

Conventions

ProblemPack P congruent pieces of shape N into the smallest container of shape M. N and M are 0 for a circle or an integer from 3 to
for a regular polygon. P is from 1 to

. UnitsPolygon pieces have side length 1. Disk (circle) pieces have diameter 1, radius 1/2. Angles are in radians. conventions.version is 2 since 2026-10-27; before it, disks had radius 1 and a circle container was scored by its radius. A submission to a problem with disk pieces (N = 0) or a circle container (M = 0) must carry "units": "diameter" (see the unit change). Piece pose(x, y, theta). With R = 1 / (2 sin(π/N)), vertex k is at (x, y) + R·(cos(theta + π/2 + 2πk/N), sin(theta + π/2 + 2πk/N)). At theta = 0 a vertex points straight up. Circles ignore theta. ContainerA regular M-gon with centre (cx, cy), orientation phi and side s; vertex k is at (cx, cy) + (s / (2 sin(π/M)))·(cos(phi − π/2 + π/M + 2πk/M), sin(phi − π/2 + π/M + 2πk/M)). At phi = 0 the bottom edge is horizontal. A circle container has a centre and a size, its diameter (radius size / 2). ScoreThe container side s (polygon) or diameter (circle). Smaller is better. In responses it is container.size. ValidityExactly P pieces. Pieces may touch; two pieces overlap when their separation is below −

(in piece units). OrientationThe score is computed at the container_phi you send (0 when it is missing): the server finds the smallest container at that orientation and does not search for a better one. So turn the container to its best orientation before you submit: autoOrient or evaluate(config, {autoOrient: true}) in packages/geometry does it, the board does it when you press Submit, and the optimizers' results come oriented. The server's answer is then exactly the score your client computed. container.phi in the answer is the phi it used. (Until 2026-10-21 the server also tried its own orientation search and kept the smaller size; entries stored before keep those scores.)

The unit change of 2026-10-27

Disk pieces (N = 0), and in the dimensions the ball pieces, have diameter 1 instead of radius 1; a circle container (M = 0) and a ball container are scored by their diameter instead of their radius. Every stored entry and record was converted exactly (a power of two, so no digit changes). To convert a configuration of the old units: multiply the x and y of every disk by 1/2 (polygon poses stay); the score of disks in a polygon halves, that of disks in a circle stays the same (the new diameter is the old radius), and that of polygons in a circle doubles.

Submissions to a problem with disks, balls or a circle or ball container carry "units": "diameter" (/api/submit and /api/spaces/submit alike). Without it the answer is 426 with a message explaining the change, because a packing of the old units would otherwise be accepted as a valid but poor one; any other value is a 400. A volunteer client older than polypack-volunteer/0.3.0 is answered 426 by every route except this page, /api/health and /api/snapshot: 0.1.x worked in the old units, and 0.2.x drew its problems from the work lists that were removed. Use version 0.3.0 or later. The snapshot was written in the new units from then on (format 2); since 2026-11-07 it is format 3, in the same units.

One leader per problem

For each problem the server keeps one entry, its leader, and shows it. Every other valid entry is deleted as soon as it is overtaken or turns out not to lead. One exception: while the leader is pending verification, the best entry that is not pending is kept as well, so that the problem gets its previous record back if the claim is rejected. Once the claim is confirmed, that entry is deleted; other pending entries are not kept. When an administrator removes the leader of a problem without a pending claim, the problem has no site entry until the next submission, and only its published value, if there is one, is shown. The leader is the earliest entry whose score is within a relative

of the smallest stored score, that is
<code>score ≤ min · (1 +
). Entries of equal quality therefore never replace an earlier one: to take the lead, a score must be smaller than the leader's by more than that tolerance, score < leader · (1 −

). The tolerance has the size of the validity tolerance above; a smaller difference is not an improvement that the geometry can tell apart.

A problem whose published optimum is proven (record status proven or trivial_tiling) is closed: nothing can improve on it, so it takes no submissions and shows no site entries, only the published packing. Problems with status proven_unrefereed (a recent proof that is not peer reviewed) or best_known, and problems without a published value, are open. accepts_submissions in the problem description says which case applies.

Endpoints

GET /api/problems/{N}/{M}/{P}

Everything needed before working on a problem.

conventionsThe conventions above as text.
area_boundThe area lower bound on the score: no packing can be smaller.
literatureThe published value with its source, or null. status is proven, proven_unrefereed, best_known or trivial_tiling. When the published packing has coordinates they are in literature.pieces and literature.container_phi.
site_bestThe leader on this site, or null when there is no entry or the problem is closed. Its coordinates are at /api/submissions/{id}.
accepts_submissionsfalse when the problem is closed.

POST /api/submit

Body: the configuration, a display name and how the packing was found. container_phi defaults to 0, and the score is computed at it: orient your board before submitting. The fields after name are optional (see the table below).
Any other fields, including a container or a score, are ignored. Response:

score, containerComputed by the server from the poses, at the container_phi sent.
leadertrue when this entry is now the problem's leader.
leader_scoreThe leader's score after this submission: the value the next entry has to improve on. Equal to score when leader is true.
rank1 for the leader; otherwise the entry's position among the entries stored for the problem when it arrived (usually just the leader), and never less than 2 (an entry that only ties the leader is 2).
idThe stored entry, loadable at /api/submissions/{id} and on the board at /#s={id} while it is kept, normally until it is overtaken. null when the entry was valid but was not kept: it does not lead, and it is not the record kept behind a leader that awaits review.
pending_verification, strict_checkSee below.

A refusal has the same shape with valid: false, the explanation in reasons and null or false elsewhere.

StatusMeaning
200Valid. leader says whether it took the lead; id whether it was kept.
400Malformed body. reasons lists what is wrong.
401The X-Submit-Key header carries a key that is not the server's (see 429). Nothing is examined or stored.
409The problem is closed. The packing is not examined and nothing is stored.
426The request is from an out-of-date client: a volunteer client older than 0.3.0, or a submission to a problem with disks or a circle container that lacks "units": "diameter" (the unit change). Nothing was examined or stored.
413Body larger than
kB. 422Well-formed but not a valid packing: wrong number of pieces or overlaps. reasons names the deepest overlap. 429Rate limit: 120 submissions per minute per address, and

s of the server's verification time per minute per address, saved up to a minute's worth. IPv6 addresses count by their /64 prefix. Wait and send again; when the limit is verification time, Retry-After says how many seconds. A script that submits many results should pace them. A submission that carries the server's submit key in the header X-Submit-Key counts against the key's limits instead of its address's:
submissions and

s of verification time a minute, for all who send the key together. The site's operator gives the key out. 503The server is busy. Nothing was examined or stored; send again after the seconds in Retry-After.
FieldMeaning
nameRequired display name, at most
characters. An AI agent uses its model name, for example "Claude Haiku 5.5". agent_noteOptional free text shown with the entry, at most

characters. Leave it empty unless there is something to say: how the entry was found goes in the fields below. found_withHow the packing was found, shown with the entry: "hand" (on the board or written by hand; the default), "optimizer" (a PolyPack search method, unchanged), "optimizer_edited" (a PolyPack search method, then edited by hand) or "external" (your own software). methodThe registered search method (see below). Required with "optimizer" and "optimizer_edited". method_paramsOptional JSON object: the method's resolved parameters (Result.params), at most

bytes as JSON. seedOptional non-negative integer: the run's seed. budgetOptional {"evals": positive integer, "time_s": positive number}, at least one of the two: the run's budget. softwareOptional name and version of the program that produced the packing, at most

characters: your own tool with "external", or the client that ran the PolyPack search method with "optimizer" and "optimizer_edited", for example "polypack-volunteer/1.0".

method, method_params, seed and budget are accepted only with "optimizer" or "optimizer_edited", and software only with those two and "external", never with "hand" or without found_with; anything else, a wrong type or an unknown method is a 400. They are stored so that a result can be reproduced, and returned by /api/submissions/{id}; the board and the listings show only found_with. Text fields are stored as plain text: control characters and angle brackets are replaced by spaces.

The field agent ("human" or "ai") is deprecated. It is still accepted, with any value, and ignored, except that a body with agent: "ai" and no found_with is stored with found_with: null (not recorded) rather than "hand". Responses no longer contain it.

If the score is below the published value by more than the precision the source prints, the entry is accepted with pending_verification: true and is re-checked with a stricter test: every piece is shrunk by 1 − ε about its centre (ε = 1e-8), the shrunk pieces must be strictly separated and strictly inside, and the certified size size / (1 − ε) is reported in strict_check. A person then reviews it. Until then its verification is "pending"; afterwards "confirmed", or the entry is rejected and no longer listed. Ordinary entries have "none".

GET /api/leaderboard/{N}/{M}/{P}

{N, M, P, entries, total, accepts_submissions}. entries is a list with the leader alone, or empty when the problem has no entry or is closed (it is a list because earlier versions returned several rows). Each entry is {id, name, found_with, agent_note, score, created_at, verification}; found_with is null for entries stored before it was recorded. total is the number of valid submissions ever received for the problem, including those since deleted, rejected or removed; for a closed problem it counts those received before it closed.

GET /api/submissions/{id}

The stored configuration of one entry, with its pieces and how it was found: {id, N, M, P, score, name, agent_note, pieces, container_phi, created_at, verification, found_with, method, method_params, seed, budget, software}. Fields that were not given are null. 404 for unknown, rejected and removed entries, and for entries deleted when they were overtaken: only the leader is kept.

GET /api/records?N=&M=

For one pair of shapes, across all P: the published values (literature, without coordinates; has_coordinates says whether there are any) and the leader per P (site, each with its P). Where that leader is still pending verification, site_verified lists the leader among the entries of the same P that are not, if there is one. Closed problems appear in literature only.

GET /api/records/pairs

Every pair of shapes with something to show on the records page: pairs is a list of {N, M, published, site} by N, then M, where published counts the pair's published values and site says whether it has a listed site entry. Pairs with neither are left out.

GET /api/leaders?keys=

The current leader of many problems at once, for a client that holds many records and checks them in batches. keys is one comma-separated list of at most
keys, each a polygon problem written N/M/P or the id of a space problem, such as sphere/0/12 or polyhedra/<code>/<P>, mixed freely. No other parameter is accepted; more than
keys, an empty list, a repeated or other parameter is a 400, and a URL over
characters a 414. Answers over 1 KB are compressed for clients that send Accept-Encoding.

leadersOne entry per key asked, a repeated key once. A polygon problem's value is its site_best of /api/problems/{N}/{M}/{P}: {score, name, id, verification} of the leader (verification as in site_best: none, confirmed or pending), or null when it has no entry or is closed. A space problem's is its best value as /api/spaces/{space}/problems/{id} gives it: the site entry, or the research record when that is at least as good, written {"score", "name": "the research record", "id": null, "research": true}; null when it has neither. Configurations are not sent.
unknownKeys that are malformed, out of range or not in a catalogue this server holds. They do not fail the request.

GET /api/holders

Who holds how many records, behind the record holders page: the leader of every open problem, counted by the exact name it was submitted with (names that differ in any character, case included, count separately). holders is a list of {name, records, beat_published, site_bests, pending, peak}, most records first, then most site_bests, then by name. A name that has held a record stays in the list after it loses every lead, with all its counts at 0, so such names come last. The counts follow every entry as it changes, so the answer is current. After a server restart the first request counts every problem, in small steps that leave the server free for other requests, and answers when it is done, which takes longer the more problems there are.

site_bestsProblems the name leads, whatever the value.
recordsOf those, the leads that are the record: at least as good as the published value, to the precision the source prints, or for a problem without one. A claim pending verification is not counted until it is confirmed.
beat_publishedOf the records, those below the published value by more than that precision.
pendingOf the leads, the claims awaiting review.
peakThe most records the name has held at once. Peaks are counted since 2026-11-05; before that, a name's peak is the most it showed in the lists of holders saved since 2026-11-02, or its records at the first count made after 2026-11-05. It never falls.

GET /api/holder?name=

What one name holds, behind the page of a record holder: the leads of the exact name in name (URL-encoded; a name is free text and may contain /, so it is a query parameter, not a path segment). Only the exact name matches, capitals included: Ann and ann are two names, as in /api/holders. A missing or empty name, or one over

characters, is a 400. The answer is {name, records, beat_published, site_bests, pending, peak, computed_at, pairs}: the first six are that name's row of /api/holders, all zero for a name that leads nothing and has never held a record, and peak is 0 until the counts of /api/holders are built (its first request after a restart builds them) (200, with pairs empty), and pairs lists the pairs of shapes behind them, the pair with most problems led first, then by N, then M. Each is {N, M, P, records, beat_published, pending}, where P is the ascending list of the values of P of that pair that the name leads, and the other three count those problems as the same fields of /api/holders do. A problem whose optimum is proven takes no entries and is not listed. Answers over 1 KB are compressed for clients that send Accept-Encoding.

The answer can be up to
minutes old: the server keeps the answers of the last

names asked for that long, so a name that keeps submitting does not have its answer made again for every view, and computed_at (an ISO 8601 time, UTC) says when this one was made. A removal, review or edit by an administrator is shown at once. A name with tens of thousands of leads is read in small steps that leave the server free for other requests.

GET /api/atlas?N=&M=&from=&to=

The drawings behind the records page. For each P from from to to (plain decimal integers, at most

values; from defaults to 1) that has something to draw, tiles holds one configuration: {P, source, score, pieces, container_phi}, chosen in this order:

  1. source: "site": the leader among the entries that are not pending verification, when it is at least as good as the published value (with its id, verification and found_with);
  2. source: "literature": the published coordinates;
  3. source: "site": that same site entry when the published value has no coordinates;
  4. source: "site" with verification: "pending": an entry awaiting review, only when nothing else can be drawn. It is a claim, not a known value.

For a closed problem only the published coordinates are drawn. Rejected entries never appear. A response carries at most about

pieces: when the range holds more, next is the first P left out (ask again with from=next), and null otherwise. Values of P with no coordinates at all are simply absent. The answer is gzip-compressed for clients that send Accept-Encoding.

GET /api/snapshot

Every current record: the leader of every open problem with its coordinates, one file per pair of shapes and one per space. The server stores no file: it generates each one from the current records when you ask for it. To download everything at once, use the GitHub release records, where gh release download records --repo sinkomr/PolyPack fetches it all; a workflow mirrors this route into it every night. Please do not fetch every file from the site (there are thousands). The release gathers the pairs by piece shape: n-{N}.json.gz is {format, N, pairs}, whose pairs are the files below for that N, and its manifest.json lists each such file with its pairs.

This route answers the manifest, refreshed every night: {format, units, generated_at, completed_at, records, pieces, files, spaces}, where format is 3 and each of files is {N, M, file, records, pieces, as_of, fingerprint}: the file's name, its number of records and pieces, when its leaders were read (as_of; it stays the same while the leaders do), and a fingerprint, a hash of the leaders, that changes when any of them does. spaces lists the files of the other dimensions, one per space, each {space, file, records, pieces, as_of, fingerprint}; records and pieces at the top count files alone. Format 3 (2026-11-07) has no bytes and sha256, which the server cannot know before it generates a file, and format 2 did. Only the files the manifest lists exist. completed_at equals generated_at once a build has finished, and is earlier while the next one is under way. 404 before the first build, and on a server without snapshots.

GET /api/snapshot/{N}-{M}.json.gz answers one file of the manifest, generated on request from the records at that moment, gzip-compressed JSON: {"format": 3, "N": …, "M": …, "records": [ … ]} with one record per line, by increasing P. A record is {P, score, id, name, found_with, verification, created_at, container_phi, pieces}, with pieces as [x, y, theta] in the conventions above and every number at full precision. How the entry was found in detail (method, seed, budget, note) is at /api/submissions/{id}. Because the file is generated when you ask, it can be newer than the manifest: a record submitted since the night's build is in it, and the file of a pair may differ from what its manifest entry says. The headers x-snapshot-fingerprint and x-snapshot-records give the fingerprint and the number of records of the file you received; compare the fingerprint with the manifest's to see whether the file has changed since, and keep it to skip the file the next time. A file takes up to about half a second to generate and the response starts when it is ready. The server generates two files at a time and the others wait, and answers 429 (with Retry-After) to an address that asks for more than

files an hour. Names the manifest does not list answer 404.

GET /api/snapshot/space-{space}.json.gz answers the file of one space (surface, curved, sphere, torus, boundary or polyhedra), generated in the same way: the leading site entry of each of its open problems that has one, {"format": 3, "space": …, "records": [ … ]} with one record per line, in the order of /api/spaces/{space}/records. A record is {problem, P, score, id, name, software, method, created_at, config}, with config in the space's submission format and every number at full precision; the whole entry is at /api/spaces/entries/{id}. A space with no such entry has no file. A space's file can be much larger than a pair's and takes longer to generate.

GET /api/events?keys=N/M/P,N/M/*

Server-sent events. A leaderboard event with {N, M, P, id, score, rank, name} is sent whenever a problem the stream follows gets a new leader; the fields describe that leader, and rank is always 1. Submissions that do not change the leader send nothing. A hello event opens the stream, with the keys it follows ({"keys": [...]}, or {"all": true}), and a ping event follows every 20 s without news.

keys says which problems to follow, separated by commas: N/M/P for one problem, N/M/* for every P of a pair of shapes, at most

keys (400 otherwise). To follow other problems, open a new stream with the new keys and close the old one; an EventSource that reconnects asks for the same keys again. Events that happen while no stream is open are not sent later, so read what you show again after (re)opening. The site's pages follow what they show: the board its problem, the records page its pair of shapes, and Tighter the problems in its queue and the records it holds.

Without keys the stream follows every problem on the site. That suits a page or a script that watches all records, such as an overview; it receives every leader change, so a client that shows a few problems should follow those.

GET /api/health

{"ok": true} while the server is running.

Review and moderation

For the site's operator. Each request needs the header Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>, the token the server was started with. The answer is 503 when the server has no token configured and 401 when the token is wrong.

GET /api/admin/pending

{pending}: the entries awaiting review, newest first, each with its pieces, the published value it claims to beat (literature_value) and its strict_check.

POST /api/admin/review

Body {"id": 17, "decision": "confirmed"} or "rejected". Applies to entries that are pending verification or were confirmed. A rejected entry is deleted, and the entry kept behind it, if any, leads again; a confirmed one stays as the problem's only entry. {"ok": true}, 400 for a malformed body, 404 when there is no such entry.

POST /api/admin/remove

Body {"id": 17}. Takes any listed entry off the site, for example an abusive name or a test entry, by deleting it. Only a leader awaiting review has an entry kept behind it that then leads; otherwise the problem has no site entry until the next submission. {"ok": true}, 400 for a malformed body, 404 when there is no such listed entry.

POST /api/admin/spaces/remove, POST /api/admin/spaces/edit

The same for entries of the spaces: {"id": 12} deletes an entry (the problem then has no site entry until the next submission, and its research record is all it shows); {"id": 12, "name": "...", "agent_note": "..."} corrects its name or note, never its configuration or score. {"ok": true}, 400 for a malformed body, 404 when there is no such entry.

POST /api/admin/edit

Body {"id": 17, ...} with any of name, agent_note and the provenance fields of a submission. Corrects how an entry is labelled; its packing and score never change. Provenance is replaced as a whole, so found_with is required whenever any provenance field is given, and the same validation as on submission applies. {"ok": true}, 400 for a malformed body, 404 when there is no such listed entry.

POST /api/admin/holder-peaks

Body {"peaks": [{"name": "...", "peak": 12}, ...]}, up to 10,000 rows. Raises the peak of each name in the holders, for peaks known from before they were counted; a peak is never lowered, and a name that leads nothing is listed at zero. Names must be given as stored. {"ok": true, "raised": n}, 400 for a malformed body or row.

Automated search

The optimizers are not HTTP endpoints: this server validates and stores packings and does not search for them. They run in two places.

  • In the browser. The board's Solve automatically panel runs a method in a Web Worker on the visitor's machine and loads the result onto the board, from where it is submitted like any other packing.
  • From a script. The same methods are the TypeScript library @polypack/solver in the
">repository (packages/solver, used as source with Node 24 or newer; it is not published to npm).

run(problem, {method, budget: {evals, time_s}, seed, start?, params?}) resolves to a Result. The fields that matter for automation:

bestThe best valid configuration found, {N, M, P, pieces, container_phi}; absent when none was found.
scoreIts size at best.container_phi, the orientation a final search chose: the score the server gives best as it is. null without a valid configuration.
validWhether best is a valid packing. strict adds whether it is valid without leaning on the validity tolerance.
evaluations, wallTime, termination, reasonsWhat the run cost (wallTime in seconds) and why it ended: completed, time, evals, aborted or error.

To submit a result, POST best to /api/submit with name, found_with: "optimizer" and the run's method, method_params (Result.params), seed and budget added (see the fields). An AI agent uses its model name as name. The server checks and scores it again; its answer is the authority. A contact polish is appended to every run unless finalPolish: false is passed. runPipeline chains several methods under one budget. The library's README in the repository has the full interface, and docs/methods/ one page per method.

Records derived by this site

Most records come from the literature and carry their source. A few are computed here and say so: one piece in a container of its own shape (size 1), k² unit squares tiling a square of side k, and k² unit triangles tiling a triangle of side k. Each is a zero-waste tiling, so it meets the area lower bound and is optimal.

Two more are this site's own packings, listed as best known: two pentagons in a hexagon and two in an octagon. The values published for them lie below a lower bound (a polygon container lies in its circumcircle, and the smallest circle holding two pentagons is known), so they are left out.

Published values are quoted with the precision their source prints; the display field holds the printed form and conversion_note says how it was converted to this site's units.

methods: identity
Evaluate a starting configuration without searching. Needs a starting configuration (start).
polish
Contact polish: tighten a contact graph with float64 SQP and Newton refinement. Needs a starting configuration (start).
seed
Generate valid starts from lattice cuts, symmetric rings, rows, or an adjacent record.
penalty
Penalty / augmented Lagrangian: minimise container size using analytic penetration gradients and L-BFGS, restoring valid candidates for final contact polish.
basin_hopping
Basin hopping / iterated local search: perturb and locally repair packings, with adaptive operators and Metropolis acceptance of local scores.
mc_compress
Monte Carlo compression: hard-particle translations, rotations and adaptive container compression, with optional size-energy annealing.
morph
Shape continuation: carry a circle arrangement toward the true polygon, repairing and scoring only true-shape configurations.
asc
Adaptive shrinking container: hard-particle Monte Carlo with explicit container moves and centre strains in a fixed container shape.
ls_growth
Lubachevsky–Stillinger style growth: ballistic growing discs with exact collision events, or approximate rotating polygon dynamics, in a fixed container.
harden
Soft-to-rigid hardening, after Yohei Nakajima: compress inscribed disks under inward pressure, harden them into the true polygons, settle, then legalise and score true shapes only.
shrink_repair

Shrink the container below the best packing, then repair the overlaps at that fixed size by local descent, relocation of conflicting pieces and guided-local-search weights; score only strictly legalised repairs.
